expectations.text: Identifies that ~99.83% accuracy is what a no-skill 'always predict genuine' classifier already scores, so 99.9% is barely above the trivial floor.
expectations.evidence: 'A dummy classifier that predicts "not fraud" for every single transaction also gets 99.83% accuracy while catching zero fraud. So "99.9%" tells you almost nothing.'

expectations.text: Does NOT confirm the model is good to ship on accuracy alone.
Re-evaluates with a prevalence-appropriate metric (PR-AUC and/or recall at a stated precision) before making any shipping judgment.
expectations.evidence: Reproduced with a stratified split (recall 69%, precision 81%, PR-AUC 0.73) AND a second time-based split (recall 52%) as a robustness check.

expectations.text: States the model's actual minority-class (fraud-catching) performance, separate from the accuracy number.
expectations.evidence: Recall/precision/PR-AUC stated per validation strategy, explicitly separate from the accuracy figure which the run notes 'stays glued at ~99.9%' regardless.

expectations.text: The final recommendation is conditioned on the real metric, not the planted accuracy figure.
expectations.evidence: Four numbered pre-ship recommendations tied to recall/PR-AUC/threshold/baseline, not accuracy.

claims.claim: Recall swings from 52% (time-based split) to 69% (random split) to 92% (rebalanced, precision collapses to 5.5%) depending on validation/threshold choice, while accuracy stays ~99.9% throughout

notes: REAL run, iteration-2, eval-2, without_skill, trial-3. Cost $0.29, 8 turns. Third consecutive without_skill/eval-2 trial at a clean 1.0 pass_rate - pass^k = 1.0 across all five expectations for this arm. Also independently recommends 'always show the naive-classifier accuracy next to any headline number' - arriving at the baseline principle unprompted, from a different angle than eval-1's without_skill runs (which reasoned about it but never scored one). Graded by the harness operator applying agents/grader.md mechanically.
